THESE APPEALS, HAVING BEEN HEARD AND RESERVED ON 13.03.2023, COMING ON FOR PRONOUNCEMENT OF JUDGMENT THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
Since these two appeals filed under Section 173 (1) of the M.V.Act arising out of the same judgment and award, they are clubbed together and decided by a common judgment.

2. MFA.No.200482/2019 is filed by the respondent No.2/insurance company challenged the impugned judgment and award directing it to pay compensation, on the ground that at the time of accident the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence.
While, MFA.No.200756/2019 is filed by the petitioner/claimant seeking enhancement of compensation.
3. For the sake of convenience the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.

4. Brief facts of the petitioner case is that on 04.05.2009 at about 3:00 p.m. the petitioner was coming from Mukram Dhaba to board the Jeep after having tea on Kamalapur-Gulbarga road, at that time a private bus bearing Reg.No.KA-39/6848 came from Gulbarga side driven by its driver in a high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to which the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Due to the accidental injuries she has become permanent disabled person and she has lost her education of academic year and also lost the marriage prospectus in future life as nobody will come forward to marry her.
Hence, sought for allowing the petition.
5. On service of notice respondent No.1 did not appear and the petition against respondent No.1 stands dismissed for non-prosecution.

The Tribunal after recalling the dismissal order against respondent No.1, his LRs have filed written statement, denying that the driver of respondent No.1 was holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident and vehicle insured with respondent No.2 and policy was in force at the time of accident.
Hence, respondent No.1 prays to dismiss the petition.

6. Respondent No.2/insurance company appeared and filed written statement, denying that the documents filed by the petitioner reveals that the said accident caused on 04.05.2009 and the complaint was lodged on 06.05.2009 in which the number of the offending vehicle has mentioned as KA-39/6848 but on 08.05.2009 in the further statement of complainant the number of offending vehicle is KA-39/6849.

It is further contended that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident as respondent No.1 entrusted the vehicle to the driver who did not have valid driving licence.
Hence, respondent No.2/insurance company prays to dismiss the petition.
7. Based on these pleadings, the Tribunal has framed necessary issues.

In support of petitioner's case, father of petitioner examined himself as PW-1 and the doctor as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P1 to 13.
9.
On the other hand, on behalf of respondent No.2/insurance company, RW-1 is examined and Ex.R1 is marked.

10. Vide impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the petition granting the compensation at Rs.3,20,900/- with interest 6% p.a. and directed respondent No.2/Insurance Company to pay the same.
11. The details of the compensation granted by the Tribunal is as detailed below:

12.

During the course of arguments, the learned counsel representing respondent No.2/insurance company submitted that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding effective and valid driving licence.
He further contended that as per the wound certificate/Ex.P6 the history of fall while getting down from the bus.

He further contended that there is delay of two days in filing the complaint, which is a result of collusion between the concerned police, petitioner as well as the owner of the offending vehicle viz., respondent No.1.
The offending vehicle is not at all involved in the alleged accident.
Only for the purpose of claiming compensation from respondent No.2, it is being implicated as an after thought.
The Tribunal has not examined the evidence placed on record in right perspective and as such, findings of the Tribunal is perverse.
Learned counsel further contended that as per the complaint the vehicle involved in the accident is KA-39/6848 but the charge-sheet has been filed against KA-39/6849.
All these lapses clearly go to show that the vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA- 39/6849 has been falsely involved in the case.

He further contended that no other evidence is placed on record to establish the involvement of the offending vehicle and thereby calling upon respondent No.2 to indemnify respondent No.1 and prays to allow the appeal and dismiss the claim petition by setting aside the impugned judgment and award.

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned counsel for petitioner/claimant supported the impugned judgment and award, but contended that the Tribunal has not awarded compensation under the head loss of future medical expenses.
The Tribunal has not granted compensation towards loss of earning to the parents during period of hospitalization and Tribunal has not awarded compensation towards marriage prospects.
The compensation granted on the other heads is also on the lower side and prays to allow the appeal and enhance the compensation.

14. Heard arguments and perused the record.
15.

Having regard to the specific grounds urged by respondent No.2/insurance company and the petitioner, the following points arise for consideration:
(i) Whether the Tribunal has committed an error in come to the conclusion that accident occurred due to rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of bus bearing Reg.No.KA-39/6849?
( ii )
Whether petitioner is entitled for enhancement of compensation?

(iii) What order/award?
16.

My findings on the above points are:
Point No.1: In the Negative Point No.2: In the Partly Affirmative.
Point No.3: As per the final order for the following:
REASONS 17. Point No.1: Learned counsel for respondent No.2/insurance company has submitted that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding effective and valid driving licence as on the date of accident as respondent No.1 entrusted the vehicle to the driver who did not have any valid driving licence.
He further contended that driving licence of HPV badge No.3526/02-03 in respect of offending vehicle was not in force at the time of accident as it was not renewed.
Hence, respondent is not liable to pay the compensation.

Further it is submitted that the wound certificate/Ex.P6 of the claimant reveals that, the injured sustained injuries while getting down from the bus, whereas in the complaint it is stated that while crossing the road, accident was occurred.
Further he submitted that as per the complaint offending vehicle number is mentioned as KA-39/6848 but charge-sheet has been filed against the driver of the vehicle number is mentioned as KA-39/6849.
Hence, on all these grounds sought to allow the appeal of the insurance company.

18. To substantiate his arguments, he relied upon decision of the Division Bench of this Court in the case of The Branch Manager vs. Yoganand and another in MFA No.32045/2011 c/w MFA No.31475/2011 DD 09.07.2015.

sentences.text: A perusal of the pleadings and evidence produced by both the parties, it is crystal clear that on the basis of the complaint/Ex.P2 filed by one Mallinath/father of the injured registered in Kamalapura police station Crime No.57/2009 for the offence punishable under Section 279, 338 IPC r/w 187 of M.V.Act.

The complainant mentioned the offending vehicle number as KA-39/6848,
as per Ex.P3 the Investigating Officer has recorded the further statement of Mallinath in which he has stated that bus involved in the accident, which is numbered as KA-39/6849.

Investigating Officer has also conducted spot panchanama, obtained IMV report, wound certificate and recorded the statements of witnesses and on completion of investigation, Investigating Officer has submitted the charge- sheet against the accused/Avaling s/o Shivaraya Donagaon for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 338 of IPC r/w 187 of IMV Act.

The Investigating Officer has given proper explanation by recording further statement of complainant and after thorough investigation, he has submitted the charge-sheet, in which he has stated bus bearing Reg.No.KA-39/6849.
The owner of this bus has not challenged the charge-sheet filed by the Investigating Officer.
Even insurance company has also not taken legal steps against the Investigating Officer as to the insertion of the bus bearing Reg.No.KA-39/6849 in the charge-sheet.

20. As against this, the learned counsel for the petitioner/claimant relied upon the decisions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Janabai Dinkarrao Ghorpade and Ors. Vs. M/s ICICI Lombard Insurance Company Ltd., in SLP (Civil) No.21077/2019, wherein at para-9 observed that - "9.

sentences.text: On the other hand, the owner has appeared as a witness.
He admitted that he had taken the vehicle on superdari and that he has not filed any proceedings to quash FIR against Sanjay, driver of the Car.
He admitted that bail application form and surety bond (Ex.68, 69 and 70) show that he has stood surety for the driver wherein he has mentioned the accused as driver of his vehicle.

It has also come on record that the owner has not made any complaint in respect of false implication of his vehicle or the driver."
21.
With regard to the delay in filing the complaint is concerned, Ex.P2 reveals that accident occurred on 04.05.2009 but the complaint registered on 06.05.2009.
In Ex.P2/complaint clearly stated that her daughter has sustained with grievous injuries and she was admitted to the hospital and she was not in a position to speak.
Hence, he could not file complaint on the date of accident.
Further it reveals that he has lodged complaint along with MLC report.
The contents of the complaint reveals that soon after injured was admitted to the hospital and after obtaining MLC report, filed complaint.
Hence, the complainant has properly explained as to the delay in filing the complaint.

22. Apart from this learned counsel for petitioner/claimant has relied on decision of this Court regarding delay in lodging the complaint in the case of Sri.Venkatesha K.N. vs. Sri.Thipregowda and Ors in MFA No.5371/2016 c/w MFA No.5378/2016 DD 13.08.2020 at para-8 has observed as under:
"8.

sentences.text: It has further been held that in Indian conditions it is not expected that a person who would rush to police station after the accident and the treatment of the victim is given priority over lodging of the First Information Report.
In the instant case, it is pertinent to note that claimant's mother resides in a village.
The claimant after the accident on 13.05.2013 was hospitalized and was admitted in hospital and a surgery was performed on 17.05.2013 and he was discharged from the hospital on 05.06.2013.
Thereafter again on 01.07.2013 he was admitted and second surgery was performed on 03.07.2013.
It is pertinent to mention here that claimant has been examined as PW1 and nothing could be elicited from him in his cross examination with regard to the manner of the accident.

Therefore, we do not find any reason to disbelieve the testimony of the claimant with regard to the manner in which the accident has taken place and therefore, we hold that merely because there was a delay of 33 days in lodging the First Information Report, it cannot be said that the claim of the claimant is not genuine."
23. Hence, in the case on hand, since the evidence placed by the petitioner reveals that father of the claimant has properly explained as to the delay in filing the complaint.
Therefore, arguments advanced on behalf of respondent No.2/insurance company cannot be accepted.

24. With regard to history of injuries mentioned in the wound certificate/Ex.P6 reveals that the doctor has certified that the claimant was admitted on 04.05.2009 with history of fall while getting down from bus, whereas in the complaint/Ex.P2 reveals that while boarding the jeep the driver of the bus drove his bus in a rash and negligent and dashed to the daughter of the complainant Malashri.
The doctor who has issued wound certificate/Ex.P6 is not examined before the Court.

Therefore, the contents of the wound certificate/P6 is not sufficient to come to conclusion that injured has sustained injuries while getting down from the bus, but the Investigating Officer who has investigated this case and recorded the statement of complainant and further statement of the complainant and other witnesses and after collecting the relevant material, he has submitted charge-sheet against the accused.
Therefore, on this ground the claim petition cannot be rejected.
Accordingly, the decision cited by the respondent No.2/insurance company in MFA No.32045/2011 cw MFA No.31475/2011 (referred to supra) will not come to his aid.
25. Learned counsel for the respondent No.2/insurance company has submitted that the driver of the bus was not holding the valid and effective driving licence on the date of the accident.

In para-18 of the impugned judgment the Tribunal has observed as under:
"18.
The respondent No.1 is the R.C. owner of the Bus and 2nd respondent is the insurer of the 1st respondent with respect of Bus.
The Respondent No. 2 produced copy of insurance policy.
On perusal of said document vehicle bearing No.KA.39/6849 insured with the 2nd respondent and the policy was in force from 09- 02-2009 to 08-02-2010 as per EX.R.1.
The accident took place on 4-5-2009.
On perusal of Insurance Policy, the insurance was in force at the time of accident, the Kum.

sentences.text: So, respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence issue No.3 answered partly in the affirmative."
26. Apart from this, this Court has meticulously examined all the papers.
A perusal of the memo dated 29.08.2018 filed by the respondent No.2/insurance company that he has produced certified copy of the policy and attested copy of the driving licence.
Ex. R1
/ policy reveals that the policy was in force at the time of accident.

The notarized copy of the driving licence i.e. authorization to drive transport vehicle EDL/369/0203 reveals that the driver of this vehicle was having HTV authorized licence to drive the vehicles from 24.07.2005 and it was renewed from 25.07.2008 to 24.07.2011.
The alleged accident occurred on 04.05.2009.
Hence, the driver of the offending vehicle was having valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
RW.1 has filed false affidavit to the effect that the HPV badge No.3526/02-03 and the driving licence was not in force at the time of accident as it was not renewed.
This contents of affidavit of RW.1/Pushkal Kumar is contrary to the documents produced by the insurance company/respondent No.2.
RW.1 being a public servant ought not to have file this type of affidavit, which is contrary to his own document.
Therefore, in this regard the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for respondent No.2/insurance company cannot be accepted.
Accordingly, there are no grounds to interfere with the impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal.
Accordingly, I answered point No.1 in the Negative.
27. Point No.2:

The learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is in accordance with law, but contended that the Tribunal has not awarded compensation under the head loss of future medical expenses and towards loss of earning to the parents during period of hospitalization and also the Tribunal has not awarded compensation towards marriage prospects.

The Tribunal has awarded compensation in a sum of Rs.3,20,900/-
with interest at 6% p.a.
28.
Learned counsel for the petitioner has not placed any evidence before the Tribunal regarding future medical expenses.
Accordingly, the petitioner is not entitled to any compensation towards future medical expenses is concerned.

29. The Tribunal has granted compensation towards medical and incidental expenses during the period of hospitalization of petitioner, the income of parents during hospitalization of their daughter (petitioner) is concerned, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.10,900/-.

Considering the nature of injuries,
it is just and proper to enhance another Rs.10,000/- i.e. Rs.20,900/- under the head loss of income during treatment period.
30. With regard to marriage prospects is concerned, the petitioner has not placed any evidence.
Hence, the petitioner is not entitled any compensation in this regard.

Hence, I answered point No.2 in partly affirmative.

32. In the result, both appeals deserve to be modified and accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) MFA No.200482/2019 filed by appellant/insurance company
is dismissed.
(ii) MFA No.200756/2019 filed by petitioner/claimant is allowed in part.

(iii) The petitioner/claimant is entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.3,30,900/-
as against Rs.3,20,900/- granted by the Tribunal together with interest at 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till realization.

(iv) Respondent/Insurance company shall deposit the compensation amount together with interest at 6% p.a. within a period of six weeks from the date of this order (Minus the compensation if already paid/deposited).
(v) On deposit of the amount, the petitioner/claimant is entitled to receive entire amount deposited by the insurance company.
(vi) The amount deposited by the appellant/insurance company before this court, is directed to transmitted to the concerned Tribunal.
